records.name: Cataluña/Catalunya
records.current_summary: Assessed materially in line with the national position. No region-specific adverse incident, ordinance or enforcement finding was identified in the country dossier for this region (it sits outside the general inventory's flagged set). no region-specific incident, ordinance or enforcement finding was identified in the dedicated country dossier for this region; no sub-national facility, expression or assembly restriction exists anywhere in the country, and the 2023 national trans-equality law's implementation (including its education-facing parts) falls to the regional government. The national victimisation baseline applies here: a 2026 federation report found 44% of LGTBI respondents had experienced a hate-motivated incident. The region does contain one of the country's densest, most visible LGTBI urban centres with dedicated hate-crime structures within its own regional police force - the dossier's overall point being that in this country the fault line is city-versus-rural, not region-versus-region.

sources.claim: State Law 4/2023 of 28 February 2023 (BOE no. 51, 1 March 2023), the 'Law for the real and effective equality of trans people and the guarantee of the rights of LGBTI persons' (the 'Trans Law'), applies uniformly across Spain's autonomous communities, including this one: Title II allows adults to rectify their registered sex marker by simple declaration, with no requirement of prior medical diagnosis or treatment, and provides for corresponding document adaptation. The law further mandates public-policy, workplace, health and education measures, and its transitory provisions govern rectification applications pending at entry into force.

Human Rights Watch (16 February 2023) reports the Spanish Congress of Deputies' passage of the Trans Law: legal gender recognition by self-identification through a simple administrative process, replacing the previous requirements of a gender-dysphoria diagnosis and two years of medical treatment. The same law expands access to assisted reproduction, strengthens sexuality education, bans medically unnecessary normalising surgery on intersex children before consent, enables parental recognition for unmarried same-sex couples, and prohibits LGBTI discrimination in healthcare, employment and housing; children from age 12 can obtain recognition under conditions, a provision that proved contentious. HRW places the reform within European and international standards against disproportionate requirements for legal gender recognition.

sources.title: BOE-A-2014-11990 — Ley 11/2014, de 10 de octubre, para garantizar los derechos de lesbianas, gays, bisexuales, transgéneros e intersexuales y para erradicar la homofobia, la bifobia y la transfobia (Cataluña, BOE)
sources.claim: Official gazette text of Catalonia's own LGTBI-rights statute, Ley 11/2014 of 10 October 2014 (Generalitat de Catalunya; DOGC núm. 6730, 17 October 2014), the autonomous law after which the 2010s wave of Spanish regional LGTBI laws followed. It defines direct, indirect and association-based discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or sex characteristics, and obliges Catalan public administrations to establish mechanisms so that administrative documentation reflects gender identity. It extends protections across education, health, employment and sport (including broadening the Observatorio Catalán del Deporte to action against violence and discrimination in sport) and guarantees same-sex partners' participation in death procedures such as body identification, burial and handling of personal effects. Article 35 sanctions minor breaches by reference to the indicador de renda de suficiencia de Catalunya (between seven days' and three months' worth); Article 38 places the sanctioning regime under the department competent for LGBTI non-discrimination, with the Síndic de Greuges able to instigate proceedings.

sources.title: Derechos LGBT en España (Spanish Wikipedia, national framework context)
sources.claim: Framework-context source naming this jurisdiction: the national article records two Catalonia-firsts inside the Spanish framework — the 30 June 1998 Ley de Parejas of Catalonia, which it calls the first Spanish couples law allowing homosexual couples minimum legal provisions, and the Generalitat de Catalunya's 2014 law (Ley 11/2014) that prompted the 2010s wave of autonomous LGTBI laws — the basis of this record's treatment of the region as the national front-runner. It also dates the state framework governing the region: same-sex marriage since 2 July 2005, the 2007 gender-identity law, and the Ley 4/2023 trans law approved in February 2023 (registered sex change from age 16 without medical reports or hormonal treatment), whose implementation falls to the regional government. Operative regional instrument: Ley 11/2014 de Cataluña.

records.name: Castilla-La Mancha
records.current_summary: Not individually flagged by the country dossier in any respect: no region-specific law, incident, ordinance or enforcement finding was identified for this region either way (and it is not one of the regions the dossier's legislative-inventory note enumerates). The national position therefore governs: no facility, expression or assembly restriction exists at sub-national level anywhere in the country, the 2023 national trans-equality law is implemented by the regional government, and the national victimisation baseline applies - a 2026 federation report found 44% of LGTBI respondents had experienced a hate-motivated incident. The dossier's general notes place this region in the sparsely-populated interior where LGBT-visible community life is thinner than in the big cities.

sources.claim: State Law 4/2023 of 28 February 2023, the national 'Trans Law' for the real and effective equality of trans people and the guarantee of LGBTI rights, applies uniformly across Spain's autonomous communities, including this one: adults may rectify the registered sex entry without prior surgical reassignment, the right to the registered change being grounded in the free development of personality (art. 10.1 CE). The law further defines and sanctions discriminatory conduct and harassment on grounds of sexual orientation, sexual identity, gender expression and sexual characteristics, declares discriminatory contract clauses null and void, obliges discrimination data collection broken down by the causes covered, and mandates measures adapted to rural circumstances - the national framework the regional position in this record rests on.

Human Rights Watch (16 February 2023) on the Spanish Congress's passage of the national Trans Law: legal gender recognition by self-identification through a simple administrative process, replacing the previous gender-dysphoria diagnosis and two years of medical treatment requirements; children from age 12 may obtain recognition under conditions, a provision that proved contentious. The law also strengthens protections for unmarried same-sex couples and combats LGBTI discrimination in healthcare, employment and housing. These are the national provisions this autonomous community implements under the same framework.

records.name: Cantabria
records.current_summary:
Under Spain's Law 4/2023, gazette-published, the administrative and education-facing provisions of the national trans-equality law are implemented by the autonomous communities — Cantabria's government among them; the 2023 gender-recognition reform (self-declaration from age 12, no medical diagnosis) drew an international rights body to place the country among autonomy-first jurisdictions.

The surviving record contains no Cantabrian statute, ordinance, enforcement series or incident finding; the region's relevance to a visitor lies in implementation posture under the same national framework, not in separate restriction.

sources.claim: Washington Blade (10 April 2025) on the national framework binding every province: activists describe Argentina's trans community in a 'chaotic, desperate situation' under Milei; the federal anti-discrimination agency INADI has been closed, the Women, Gender and Diversity Ministry eliminated, and trans people hired under the public-sector labour-inclusion quota dismissed in 2024. Violence, discrimination and poverty affecting the trans community are reported as worsened; this region carries no separate reporting, so the national picture stands as its baseline.

Agencia Presentes (19 March 2026) on the National LGBT+ Hate Crimes Observatory's 2025 report: at least 227 hate crimes based on sexual orientation or gender identity in Argentina in 2025 - up 62% year on year, the highest count in the observatory's ten years of operation, one crime every 38 hours - with trans women and travestis 62.5% of victims (142 cases) and gay men 22% (50). The report ties the surge to institutional weakening and state legitimation of discriminatory discourse; this province sits under that national pattern with no separate local record.

records.name: Chaco
records.current_summary:
No Chaco-specific trans statute, quota-compliance finding or enforcement series survives in the record. The framework is national: a April 2025 national feature described the trans community facing a 'chaotic, desperate situation' after decree roll-back of the Gender Identity Law, and a national hate-crime observatory reported 227 SOGI-motivated hate crimes for 2025 — up 62% year-on-year, its highest decade count, one every 38 hours, most attackers security-force personnel or unidentified — a baseline applying across the provinces including this one.

Visitor exposure in Chaco therefore tracks the national position: no provincial criminalisation survives in the record, amid a documented national surge in anti-trans violence and a contested federal law.
records.current_localsOnly: The provincial travesti/trans employment quota for public administration is a resident-facing hiring rule; a visitor never invokes it.
